title: The canonical finite-coefficient ambient exchange on a commutative square
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring and let g′:X′ → X, p′:X′ → Y′, p:X → Y and g:Y′ → Y be a commutative square of schemes. Define its ambient exchange R p_* then L g* → L g′* then R p′_* as the mate, under the specified derived geometric adjunctions, of the derived pullback comparison obtained from the two pullback compositors and the equality p′;g = g′;p. This is the existing unit-square-counit construction before any properness or invertibility assertion.

source.place: Coefficient transport and clauses (2)--(3), canonical-map identifications.

proof.text: Form the isomorphism from Lg* followed by Lp′* to Lp* followed by Lg′* using the inverse first compositor, equality of composite scheme maps, and second compositor. Apply Mathlib mateEquiv to the specified derived pullback/direct-image adjunctions. This constructs the natural transformation and uses no chosen inverse to a geometric arrow.
